newsitem.title: UK: HK stocks in London weak in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks in London weak in cautious trade.

text.p: Hong Kong shares trading in London were lower across the board on Wednesday but most market players chose to stay on the sidelines awaiting key U.S. data later in the week.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index was off 43.73 points at 12,092.59 by 1353 GMT, pulled down to the day's lowest levels alongside a falling FTSE 100 index ahead of the opening in New York.
In Hong Kong, stocks had staged a rebound after three days of losses to finish 62.13 points ahead at 12,136.32.
"The market was holding reasonably steady until the FTSE started coming off and Hong Kong bank was hit," said one trader. "That took the rest of the market lower."
HSBC Holdings was trading at HK$176.5 in London compared to a Hong Kong close of HK$177.5.
"We haven't seen any selling pressure," the trader said. "Most people are sitting and watching, they are being very cautious at the moment."
